title: Failover dashboards + burn-rate alert rules (regional impairment + automation outcomes)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Adds versioned dashboard pack and alert rules for regional failover automation: signal panels (reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity headroom, policy flips/rollbacks) and outcome panels (failover time-to-mitigate, request shedding, Dedicated drain progress). Introduces multi-window burn-rate alerts for region impairment detection with annotations tuned for on-call triage. Includes rollout notes for staging -> prod enablement ahead of Q1 controlled failover game day.
description:
Summary: This PR adds the first versioned "Failover Signals & Outcomes" observability bundle to observability-pack. The bundle includes (1) Grafana dashboards (JSON) for diagnosing region-level impairment vs. local/service-level issues, and (2) Prometheus/Alertmanager rule groups for fast-detection burn-rate paging + non-paging early-warning signals. The intent is to support the Regional Failover Automation Upgrade (ENG-2411) by giving on-call deterministic visibility into the trigger hierarchy signals and the automation controller’s behavior (recommendations, executions, rollbacks).

What’s included: Dashboards: failover-signals-overview.json (top-level entry): reachability probe success rate and p95/p99 latency by region pair; 5xx and timeout burn (fast/slow windows); tail latency burn for key API routes; capacity headroom (fleet available vs. target) and "capacity gating" state; automation controller action rate (recommend/execute/rollback) and per-tenant safety limit hits; policy flip history with dashboard annotations (from audit events) to correlate with spikes; API gateway overload responses (429/503 w/ Retry-After) to validate graceful degradation behavior. hosted-api-failover-drilldown.json: route/model slice panels (kept intentionally low-cardinality) plus request volume shifts during failover. dedicated-drain-progress.json: drain state, queued in-flight requests, and drain completion percent (hooked to new drain progress metrics emitted in redwood PR-19842).

Alert rules: rules/failover_burn_rate.yaml: Multi-window, multi-burn alerts for region impairment (fast: 2m/10m, slow: 30m/2h) across 5xx+timeouts, aligned to the multi-region availability SLO measurement approach. The goal is quick detection without noisy flaps; each alert includes runbook_url and dashboard_url annotations. rules/failover_reachability.yaml: Pages only when synthetic cross-region probes fail AND error/latency corroboration indicates likely regional impact (prevents false positives from probe-only issues). rules/failover_controller_health.yaml: Non-paging warning for missing signal streams / stale region health ingestion, plus paging on controller crashloop or sustained decision evaluation errors.

Important implementation notes: Label/cardinality constraints: Dashboards and rules assume the reduced failover_reason/trigger_source label set from redwood PR-19829. This PR intentionally does NOT add any new high-cardinality dimensions. Where we need per-tenant visibility, we use (a) sampled logs links and (b) controller audit events with tenant identifiers in the event payload (not as metric labels). Annotations: Adds an annotation datasource/query template that reads failover audit events (recommend/execute/rollback) so timelines are visible on signal charts. This addresses INT-1149 (missing annotations during rehearsal) and makes postmortems easier to write.

Rollout/versioning: Version tag: failover-pack v2026.01.0 (directory naming + dashboard UID prefixes). Staging rollout: enable in staging first; confirm panels populate for us-east <-> eu-west, validate burn alerts in "recording" mode (no paging) for 24h. Production rollout: enable dashboards immediately; keep the two fastest burn alerts in paging mode only after go/no-go checklist confirms (a) region health ingestion stable and (b) probe data present. A toggle is provided via alert routing labels to direct to #oncall-sre-nopage during initial bake. Backward compatibility: If audit event stream is unavailable, dashboards degrade gracefully (annotations empty). If dedicated drain metrics are not present, the Dedicated dashboard panels show "no data" without errors.

Files/areas changed (high level): dashboards/failover/failover-signals-overview.json; dashboards/failover/hosted-api-failover-drilldown.json; dashboards/failover/dedicated-drain-progress.json; alerts/failover/rules/failover_burn_rate.yaml; alerts/failover/rules/failover_reachability.yaml; alerts/failover/rules/failover_controller_health.yaml; docs/rollout-notes/failover-pack-v2026.01.0.md; dashboards/_shared/annotation-templates/failover-audit-events.json.

Validation: Imported dashboards into staging Grafana and verified queries against staging metrics for the region health service + perf canary probe series. Ran promtool check for rule syntax; simulated burn alerts by replaying a short window of elevated 5xx in a test environment. CI: lint + jsonnet formatting + promtool passed.

Related: ENG-2418 (Add failover metrics and SLO burn alerts), ENG-2421 (Game day 1), redwood PR-19816 (SLO-friendly aggregations), redwood PR-19824 (audit events), perf-canary PR-188 (cross-region reachability probes), redwood PR-19829 (metric label cardinality reduction).

Review notes: Allison requested we split paging vs. non-paging signals; done by separating rule groups and adding routing labels + explicit severity guidance. Aisha requested we align burn windows with SLO reporting; updated to match the standard fast/slow burn approach and added recording rules for regional availability burn. Miles requested the trigger hierarchy be readable from the dashboard top row; added a "signal stack" row with reachability -> 5xx -> latency -> capacity, plus links to the runbook. Tomáš requested clearer runbook ownership and a single canonical dashboard link; added runbook_url and dashboard_url to all alerts.

Changelog (squash): 1) Add initial dashboards (signals overview, hosted drilldown) 2) Add burn-rate rules + annotations 3) Add dedicated drain progress dashboard 4) Tune queries + thresholds; add rollout notes; promtool + uid fixes.

Outcome: Merged. Ready to deploy to staging immediately; production enablement pending go/no-go approval for the controlled failover window.
